bilateralMainDecisions.entity: The candidate asks for the machine-readable barcode pattern as a general object; the peer asks for the retail item bought in a specific 1974 event.
bilateralMainDecisions.relation: Candidate relation is name/definition of a representation read by an optical scanner. Peer relation is an item being the first purchase scanned by a UPC scanner.
bilateralMainDecisions.value: Candidate key is «Штрихкод»; peer key is «Упаковка жевательной резинки Wrigley's». Neither is the answer to the other question.
bilateralMainDecisions.context: Generic terminology and scanner-readable pattern versus a named historical supermarket transaction. UPC is a barcode system, so they share a real topical concept; this question does not ask for the UPC system’s historical first item.
bilateralMainDecisions.directAndReverse: The candidate does not ask which item was scanned first, and the peer does not ask what the bars-and-spaces pattern is called. A respondent who knows one fact cannot derive the other answer from it. Keep both as distinct, genuinely related questions.

bilateralMainDecisions.directAndReverse: The card is not the first product purchase, and the gum package is not the credential that links Halifax loans to an account. Shared barcode/scanner vocabulary does not merge the requested entities or relations.
